title: ActGov: Governing LLM Agent Actions via Policy-Constrained Validation
summary: ActGov replaces static, predefined execution plans and fixed allowlists with a runtime enforcement layer that validates every proposed tool call against an iteratively constructed, SMT-verified policy set before external effects occur. It costs the engineering effort of building and maintaining tool specifications and policy records, plus per-action validation latency (including SMT counterexample checks during policy construction) added to each step of the agent loop. It can fail where tool specifications are incomplete or policies under-constrain authorization, where the policy-construction pipeline misses failure modes not present in observed traces, and where teams lack the verification tooling and expertise to maintain the SMT-backed policy lifecycle.
rationale: For an engineer deploying tool-calling agents against prompt injection, per-action runtime validation is directly relevant, but the abstract provides no quantified overhead or attack-reduction figures, and the SMT-based policy construction pipeline demands validation of its operational burden on the reader's specific workflow before production adoption.
technique: Runtime policy validation of LLM agent tool actions
